en: R0.73K theorem: for the certified family of two-harmonic periodic shear flows, there exists a common but not explicitly quantified viscosity threshold. When \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_K\), for every \(d\in[0,1/450]\), the common circle \(|z-0.17|<0.003\) contains exactly one real, algebraically simple viscous eigenvalue; the fixed half-plane \(\operatorname{Re}z\ge0.12\) contains no other spectral points. The Riesz projections converge uniformly in operator norm, and the eigenvalue shift obeys an \(O(\varepsilon)\) upper bound; the complementary-space reduced resolvent is uniformly bounded, and the semigroup obeys a \(Ce^{0.12t}\) growth bound. The proof does not assume full norm-resolvent convergence.

en: This page retains R0.61 through R0.73K in full, comprising 127 nodes. R0.61–R0.69W advances from the reduced recurrence to rigorous annular exclusion; R0.70A–R0.71Z examines moving scales, the critical ledger, internal entry, and the complete-root boundary; R0.72A–R0.73B treats strong coupling, the critical log, collision geometry, and the complete linear Fourier--Leray row; R0.73C–I successively treats frozen Rayleigh instability, persistence of the viscous spectral cluster, transfer to a fixed positive half-plane, gain along a moving profile, nonlinear relative amplification, planar fixed-distance deviation, and the zero-window action boundary. R0.73J certifies a continuous inviscid spectral branch; within a common but not explicitly quantified viscosity threshold, R0.73K establishes the unique real algebraically simple viscous spectral branch in a common circle, operator-norm uniform convergence of the Riesz projections, an \(O(\varepsilon)\) upper bound on the eigenvalue shift, the condition number, absence of other spectral points in a fixed half-plane, and bounds on the complementary-space reduced resolvent and semigroup growth. No extrapolation is made to adiabatic tracking, nonlinearity, transverse three-dimensional dynamics, singularity, or Clay.
